transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-25
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Aiden Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM), Jenna Morales (Northfall Head of Security), Tom Reed (Platform), Priya Shah (Compliance), Liam Brooks (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Northfall is evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for LLM inference. Primary drivers: strict EU residency for certain data classes, HIPAA-like controls for clinical-feeds to a quant team, and wanting minimal raw request logs to leave the environment. They probed KMS/HSM options, RBAC and audit evidence, and asked about log redaction and sampling at ingest. Redwood AE/SE explained capabilities, fallback models, and private deployment patterns; agreed to follow up with SOC2, network diagrams, and a dedicated scoping call.

Topics: residency, KMS, log redaction, RBAC/audit evidence, private deployment topology, Dedicated capacity SLOs, data retention/tilting SLOs

Action items (also in metadata): see action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Aiden Carter (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Jenna, Tom, Priya, Liam from Northfall, and from Redwood it's me, Maya, Noah. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jenna Morales (Northfall): Hey, thanks. Doing well. We, um, we wanted to walk through our compliance gates and make sure we, yeah, we understand where logs are stored and who sees them.
[00:18] Tom Reed (Northfall): Quick context — we're building a compliance-aware assistant for portfolio analysts. Some datasets are EU-only, some have PHI-ish fields from clinical reports (we're not a hospital but partner data can include health signals), and we need to keep audit trails minimal and exportable.
[00:33] Maya Lin (Redwood SE): Got it. So you have both residency requirements and HIPAA-like controls plus tight audit and retention constraints. First question for you — which models do you expect to run? Open weights or vendor models? That affects whether KV cache or quantized runtime paths change storage.
[00:47] Priya Shah (Northfall): Mostly open models, yes, but we may use some tuned variants. We need assurance that the inference logs don't contain PII or raw prompts by default, because legal won't sign off otherwise.
[00:58] Aiden Carter: On Redwood Hosted, by default we keep request logs for X days for SLO debugging, but we can reduce retention and redact tokens. For Dedicated and Private you get more control — you can turn off raw request logging and only emit structured traces.
[01:15] Jenna Morales: When you say redact tokens, is that pre-ingest? We want PII to never touch storage outside their VPC.
[01:22] Maya Lin: That's a good callout. For private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed, so logs never leave the VPC unless you opt in. For Dedicated we support VPC peering and customer-controlled KMS for key wrapping; however the control plane is still managed — so we do retain some telemetry. We can configure token redaction at the ingress point. In Hosted, token-level redaction is offered as a configuration but we still have a short-lived audit copy for debugging unless you sign an enterprise data handling agreement.
[01:50] Tom Reed: Can you expand on the KMS options? We need HSM-backed key control and key rotation logs for audits.
[01:56] Maya Lin: Sure. We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and allow bring-your-own HSM in Private deployments. For Dedicated, we can integrate with customer's KMS; HSM is more complicated but doable via a partner link. Keys can be used for encrypting model artifacts at rest and wrapping request/response logs. We can also provide proof of access with envelope keys and key access logs.
[02:20] Priya Shah: Auditability question — we have to provide evidence to auditors that no one outside our organization saw PHI. What does Redwood's evidence bundle look like?
[02:29] Aiden Carter: We typically provide SOC2 Type II report, segmentation diagrams, access logs, and an extractable audit bundle that shows service admin ops and who accessed keys. For Private customers we can deliver more direct evidence since control plane is in-customer. We'll share our SOC2 and an example audit pack.
[02:44] Jenna Morales: Do you keep console-level logs? We don't want engineers at Redwood looking at raw prompts.
[02:50] Noah Patel (Redwood CSM): We have RBAC and least privilege on the ops side; by default ops can't pull raw request content without an internal, audited process. But I want to be clear — for Hosted there are rare SRE troubleshooting flows that can surface logs to support teams; those are logged and require approval. For Dedicated/Private that's eliminated or controlled.
[03:12] Liam Brooks (Northfall SRE): Ok and what about log retention windows — can we set per-route retention? E.g., EU routes 30 days, global debug routes 7 days.
[03:20] Maya Lin: Yes, the console supports per-model/route retention. You can also set sampling rates for request bodies vs metadata. Sampling reduces storage but you may lose some debug granularity.
[03:33] Tom Reed: Also curious about redaction: do you do token-level redaction or semantic redaction? Token-level is sometimes insufficient for structured PHI like MRNs.
[03:42] Maya Lin: We have both. Token-level redaction removes matching patterns or regexes at ingest; semantic redaction uses a small on-host model to mask PII entities before persistence. For compliance-heavy flows we typically recommend semantic redaction in a private deploy so both the model and logs never cross boundaries.
[03:58] Priya Shah: What about decrypt keys for KV cache? Our models' KV cache could contain prefixes from prompts, is that considered an artifact?
[04:05] Maya Lin: Good question. KV cache is ephemeral in-memory during inference; we do not persist full caches to disk unless you enable snapshotting for warm start. Snapshotting can be encrypted and placed in customer S3 or dedicated block that you control. We'll note that in the scoping doc.
[04:22] Jenna Morales: Suppose we want no persistent request bodies in Redwood-managed storage and only structured traces — is that possible?
[04:28] Aiden Carter: Yes, for Dedicated you can opt for metadata-only tracing. For Hosted, it's a higher bar; we can offer a restricted-logging SLA in Enterprise contracts but it still means some telemetry retained for debugging windows.
[04:44] Tom Reed: Network-wise, we need to see sample VPC peering configs, and whether Private supports air-gapped on-prem.
[04:52] Maya Lin: Private supports on-prem and VPC-only control plane. We have an on-prem bundle for air-gapped deployments — it includes a catalog of supported GPUs, a control-plane image, and guidelines for upgrade windows. For VPC peering on Dedicated we support AWS/GCP peering and private link equivalents. We'll send sample diagrams.
[05:09] Priya Shah: Are there any retained derivatives in the model outputs — e.g., generated embeddings stored for retraining? We are paranoid about embeddings leaking sensitive context.
[05:18] Maya Lin: Redwood doesn't retain embeddings by default; storing embeddings is an explicit opt-in feature for customers for search indexing. If you do store, we recommend namespace partitioning, encryption with your KMS, and retention policies. We can also recommend quantization that reduces reverse-engineering risk.
[05:33] Jenna Morales: Great. On legal we need e-discovery and legal hold capabilities — can you preserve logs on demand?
[05:40] Noah Patel: Yes, we have an archival workflow. You can freeze a route's retention and export an evidence bundle. For Private you run that inside your infra. For Hosted we export to customer-controlled bucket with audit logging.
[05:52] Tom Reed: One of our constraints is that certain teams must never have data cross-border — can we pin models to a region and have failover only within the region?
[06:01] Maya Lin: Yes, you can configure regional routing and a policy to never failover to other regions. We also support geofenced routing for tenant-aware requests. There is a tradeoff with availability; we'll need to size Dedicated capacity to meet SLOs within region.
[06:17] Jenna Morales: What about redaction accuracy? Semantic redaction false negatives are scary — do you have metrics or a way to run our test prompts?
[06:26] Maya Lin: We usually run an eval with your redaction test set during PoC. That will measure precision/recall and show edge cases. We can then tune the semantic model or add custom regexes.
[06:36] Priya Shah: Ok. For auditors we also need to show admin activity and key rotation logs; do you provide key rotation certs?
[06:43] Aiden Carter: We can provide Key Access logs and rotation events. For Private, those live in your KMS logs. For Dedicated, we can provide exported rotation records per contract.
[06:54] Liam Brooks: What about live incident response — if there's a suspected data exposure, what's the playbook and who has the authority to pull raw logs?
[07:03] Noah Patel: We have an IR playbook — only SOC/ops leads with multi-party approval can request raw logs, and every access is audited. For an incident we coordinate with customers and can provide an evidence bundle within SLA windows.
[07:18] Tom Reed: We're very interested in a tight pilot with a small EU-only subset. Probably start with Dedicated in eu-west-1 and then evaluate Private for more sensitive flows.
[07:27] Aiden Carter: Sounds reasonable. Typical path is Hosted quick test, then Dedicated pilot in-region, then Private for final production if you need full control. But if you already need air-gap, we can accelerate Private scoping.
[07:39] Jenna Morales: Two more quick items — SSO/SAML integration and RBAC scoping. We need SCIM and role separation for developer vs compliance.
[07:47] Maya Lin: We support SSO with SAML/OAuth, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC (route-level roles). For Private we can connect to your IdP inside the VPC.
[07:58] Priya Shah: Audit logs — do they include parameterized traces or raw token counts only?
[08:04] Maya Lin: Audit logs are parameterized by default; you can choose to capture token counts, latencies, model version, and structured metadata. Raw text capture is opt-in and auditable.
[08:15] Tom Reed: Any limitations on encryption-at-rest for model shards if we want to use our keys?
[08:21] Maya Lin: You can encrypt model artifacts with your key material in Private. In Dedicated we support customer-managed key wrapping (CMK). For Hosted, we manage keys but can provide customer-specific envelopes.
[08:33] Jenna Morales: Cool. I think that covers the bulk. Can you confirm the deliverables and timeline?
[08:39] Aiden Carter: Sure — we'll send: SOC2 Type II + security pack (Aiden) by 2027-06-28; VPC and private deployment diagrams + checklist (Maya) by 2027-07-02; initial Dedicated pricing and pilot SLOs (Aiden) by 2027-07-01. Tom will share sample redaction test prompts by 2027-06-30.
[08:58] Tom Reed: I'll get those over. Also can we request a small table of what features are available in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for logging and key control?
[09:06] Maya Lin: Yep we'll produce a short feature matrix.
[09:10] Jenna Morales: Thank you. This was helpful.
[09:13] Aiden Carter: Great — appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the files. Thanks everyone.
[09:17] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional noise, typical mis-hearings — e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cash"; some proper names garbled. Some timestamps are approximate.
